INTROPara-1: Vishwakarma Design Studio is a multidisciplinary design studio based out of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Started in 1995 by Karthikeyan Padmanabhan and Ruckmini Karthikeyan, partners in the business and in life, Vishwakarma Design Studio is the creative expression of the architect and product designers.
INTROPara-2: Our story is a humble one, that begins with two young architects discovering their niche in Coimbatore. Meeting at their place of work, Karthikeyan and Ruckmini began their business, Karthik and Karthik, an architectural firm with another partner and Turya Designs, a product and design practice in 1995. Over the years, the practice evolved into Vishwakarma Design Studio and Turya Designs, marking their place in the industry as reliable, creative and honest professionals. Vishwakarma Design Studio is a design practice and business that is rooted and excited to grow further over the years to come.
SOUL: The soul of our design lies in light and nature.
SOUL-PARA: Vishwakarma is known for their unique creative expression and flair to experiment with unique structures and curves as well as apply materiality and textures in their design aesthetic. The studio has undertaken a wide range of projects ranging from residences, commercial spaces, religious spaces, factories and niche projects. Vishwakarma has carved a name for their wholistic approach to design and specialises in creating the architecture, interior and furniture design of the space. Karthikeyan, the principal architect and founder has worked over 500 projects across his career till date from inception and ideation to completion.
SOUL-PARA2: We are one of the pioneers in incorporating copper, tiles and hand etched glass in their furniture, resulting in stunning works of art that is one of a kind, statement pieces. The couple run their architectural and design practice with a small and dedicated set of designers, craftsmen, artists and staff who are all invested, passionate and have a penchant for incredible ideas and dedication to perfecting their craft. With our vast expertise, gained over a period of time, we are confidently marching towards our avowed goal of attaining undisputed leadership, in this demanding field.
VISHWA-NUMBER-PARA: Since 1995, we have implemented more than 500 projects in different parts of the country, across a varied typology and style of spaces.
karthikeyan-description-1: Karthikeyan Padmanabhan is the founding architect at Vishwakarma Design Studio. After completing his bachelors in Architecture from Manipal Institute of Technology in 1987, he worked as a junior architect at Shankar and Associates. Turya Designs came to life in 1992, in Coimbatore with his wife, Ruckmini which has become Vishwakarma Design Studio today.
karthikeyan-description-2: An old school architect, learning new technology he still values the process of putting pen to paper and this is reflected in his unique and incredible designs.
Ruckmini-quote-1: LEADING A FULFILLING LIFE IS KEY TO  GROWTH AND ABUNDANCE. BALACING SPIRITUALITY FAMILY, WORK AND INTERNAL GROWTH IS INTEGRAL IN OUR LIVES AND ORGANISATION.
Ruckmini-description-1: Ruckmini Karthikeyan is the cofounder of Vishwakarma design studio and is the management brains behind the studio. She graduated with a bachelors in Architecture from NIT, Trichy in 1988. Trained as an architect but discovered her passion for numbers and took over the reigns as the managing director. She is the brains and numbers person behind the firm and drives the success of the firm and our projects.
shreya-quote-1: CREATIVE EXPRESSION IS THE FOUNDATION OF OUR SOULS.
shreya-description-1: Shreya Karthikeyan, who is a second gen spatial architect and designer who is a cross disciplinary artist and designer. Her passion and talents are spread across graphic, spatial, literature, sketching , painting and fashion and she combines them in her design practice. She serves as the creative head and practices as an architect at Vishwakarma. Apart from that she also manages creative identities and branding for the firm and for clients.
employee-para: Our team is a passionate group of individuals that are driven and motivated. They are the ones working tirelessly to make our designs and your dreams come alive. We are proud to call them our team and love how they thrive and flourish along with us and we become family. At Vishwakarma Design Studio, we believe in a wholisitic growth  for our employees and their families, and we strive to make it a joyous enviroment that helps them grow.
Service-black-para-1: At Vishwakarma Design Studio, We weave stories through our spaces and designs.
Service-black-para-2: We sail with our clients on unique journies to bring to the life spaces, brands and identities.
Service-the-brand-para: At Vishwakarma Design Studio, We weave stories through our spaces and designs. We sail with our clients on unique journies to bring to the life spaces, brands and identities.
Kayal-para: Kayal is a contemporary event space designed for weddings and intimate gatherings. Blurring the lines between the built and the unbuilt environment, we've designed and created a space that brings in the natural beauty of the areca nut palm grove with our architectural design, resulting in a beautiful space for an event.
Actcall-para: ACT Centre is a commercial space that we designed in 2006.
century-para: Century Apparels is a special project for us, a beautiful factory, workspace and establishment that is architecturally stunning especially for a garment manufacturing platform. The office is strategically located, with stunning art, custom furniture and murals designed by us, showcasing a beautiful key space that hosts buyers, sellers and clients.
century-para2: The founders of Century believe in the holistic wellbeing of their employees and staff, with state of the art quarters that have a flood of natural light and air. The office was also designed with an open space plan to integrate all levels and hierarchies of departments to foster communication and collaboration. This factory is a must visit and hallmarks of our design!
jjmills-para: JJ Mills is an interior office design that we did in 2009, with a touch of our iconic style.
springmount-para: Learning is a key aspect in every child's life, the education we receive sets us up for life, shaping the core of a person outside of their home and family. When we designed Spring Mount School, we wanted to inculcate key aspects of holistic growth in a child that fosters out of the box thinking, and a deep connection to nature which was important to the school management. We designed an elementary school which complemented an existing group of secondary and higher secondary school students.
springmount-para2: The courtyards form the core of the flow of spaces, with the classrooms around reflecting elements of water,earth,sunlight, through materiality and elemental motifs and teaching the students key, crucial aspects through the design. Our favorite feature is the usage of recycled glass soda bottles to design the railing.
egli-para: This office is a contemporary design, with a modern landscaped courtyard serving as the focal point and all other utilities revolving around it. The office inculcates a lot of natural light and ventilation, breaking away from a corporate feel and has our signature handcrafted detailing, which makes it unique.
lnbjewellers-para: This office space is designed for a wholesale jeweller merchant, which is a prominent business in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Nestled in the heart of the city, we designed this for supplier and vendor interactions and a personal cabin space for the client for his personal use and interactions with clients as well. We also included a display space to display the products and the design theme of the entire office is rustic and traditional.
precol-para: This design is the personal office of the Managing Director of the Pricol group, an enterprising group of companies. This served as his personal space for his entrepreneurial pursuits in the restaurateur business and travel industry.
precot-para: This is the corporate office of Precot, a premier spinning mill and textile and manufacturing company based in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. This office served as a apex space for their corporate interactions and testing and analysis lab for their yarn.
spmkadri-para: The key word given by the client while designing this office is to step away from the the routine and norm. We managed to pull a twist on the space with handpainted elements, panelling and adding some life to the space.
texmo-para: The office we designed for Texmo is an intimate workspace and creative think tank space for their projects and ventures. Designed to be immersed in nature and a space to step away from the norm to create and ideate.
texmo-para2: The inspiration we drew from is a cabin in the woods.
nalanda-para: The Nalanda conference center is a luxury, wellness space that is designed to host retreats and programs. Nestled under the foothills of Siruvani, this space really opens up to the natural environment, making it a perfect space to rejuvenate.
adams-para: A small bespoke tailor space for the client in Coimbatore. This intimate studio showcases custom murals, detailing such as a bowtie magazine stand as the tailors specialises in suits, and designer mirrors to accentuate the space.
anantaboutique-para: Ananta is a boutique dealing in ethnic wear and traditional clothing in Coimbatore, India.
avatharjewellers-para: Avathar jewellers are a family business dealing in gold jewellery. The showroom we did for them is warm and bright lit, with a very classic interior design.
berlyhouse-para: The Beryl House is a spectrum of green hues, with the natural environment brought inside with the courtyard and lawn, creating a beautiful home. Karthikeyan Padmanabhan, our founder and principal architect created this house with large expansive windows, allowing a ton of natural light, ventilation and a play of the form with openings and elevation to create a beautiful structure.
bharanisilks-para: Bharani silks is a legacy in the saree and pattu business for two generations, based out of Erode, Tamil Nadu. We designed and constructed a retail store fit for their expansive and large retail business, catering to a wide range of clothing and segments. Since it was a large scale business and retail space, we kept the design very simple and professional and still incorporated detailing that distinguishes it from the competitors. The interiors are also customized to highlight the different sections and types of clothing.
chiar-para: This residence is a cozy residential property for a family of three and are all expats working in different countries. They wanted an intimate, well designed and functional house that they could come back to when they visit India and wanted a colorful yet minimalistic interior. We played with the facade of the house, with insertions of light and color, making the house very light. We also infused pops of color in the common areas and had traditional attangudi flooring in the bedrooms to enrichen the space.This house is named aptly Chiaroscuro, a play of color and light.
circularhouse-para: The Circular House is a modern architectural form that is designed in a spiral with a core courtyard informing the circulation and access to the rest of the residence. This courtyard acts as a floodlight of light, cross ventilation and gathering space. Our design practice leans on core principles of our founder and principal architect that are reflected in our projects, including vernacular architecture and natural, localised typologies of design.
colorhouse-para: The Color House, a residence in Chennai, Tamil Nadu was indeed the embodiment of color.  Our brief for the home was to infuse the space with color, to show the joy and color in the lives of the  residents in the home we were creating for them. As designers we get a plethora of clients with unique stories and for the lovely family, we implemented as much color as possible in various forms throughtout the house. Our palette was built around blues and greens, with handpainted furniture, custom gond murals that wraps around the staircase, blue and teal furniture in the dining room and a golden yellow courtyard, with a primary color palette to highlight the custom cut niches.  All our projects lean on natural ventilation  and light, connecting nature and humans, which further accentuate the colors used in the space.
colorhouse-para2: The Color House is a lively intersection of color, art and stories woven through space.
coolcooper-para: Cool Copper is a retail clothing showroom based out of Coimbatore, India.
cottonblossom-para: This residence was designed by us at the earlier stages of our architectural journey, for a textile manufacturer based out of Tiruppur, India, the hub of garment manufacturing and exports.
vadavallidonuts-para: The Donuts is a chain of bakeries and confectioneries based out of Coimbatore, India. This outlet, in Vadavalli has a fun and retro theme, with 3D cupcakes we designed and made hung from the ceiling as a detail to highlight the cafe.
saidonuts-para: The Donuts is a chain of bakeries and confectioneries based out of Coimbatore, India. This outlet, in Sai baba colony, is designed with a colonial theme that is more ornate in style. This outlet is the main kitchen for the chain and is designed with their production kitchen designed for supply for all the outlets in the city.
thudonuts-para: The Donuts is a chain of bakeries and confectioneries based out of Coimbatore, India. This outlet, in Thudiyalur is designed with a tropical theme in mind.
eventdecors-para: The Tree of Life is a wedding stage design that we designed and brought to life for a lovely couple and dear friends for their special day. We customized the backdrop with props such as a wheel wagon, and custom made a brass tree backdrop to represent the beginning of the couples journey. We at Vishwakarma, love everything design, our versatility and penchant for bringing any idea to life, enables us to think out of the box and take up any project.
garmentnook-para: Garment Nook is a retail clothing boutique store designed for a client in Coimbatore with our signature style and interior detailing.
hoe-para: A residence for a family who wanted a farm life and atmosphere, we designed this with a palette of white and earthen tones, with traditional red oxide flooring as used in tamizh housing, chettinad motifs and built in thinai (traditional porch in tamizh culture) as key design elements.
iasiveedu-para: The Isai Veedu is a residence we designed for the renowned singer Sudha Raghunathan, her home a blend of traditional, classical design that is a homage to her illustrious musical career.
ishalife-para: Isha Life is a wellness and recreational centre that we designed in 2010. A holistic approach to wellness, the space encompassed a retail space, spa, gym, massage centre and restaurant serving healthy food. Our signature elements and handcrafted feel throughout the space makes it truly one of a kind.
ishaschool-para: The office we designed for Texmo is an intimate workspace and creative think tank space for their projects and ventures. Designed to be immersed in nature and a space to step away from the norm to create and ideate. The inspiration we drew from is a cabin in the woods.
kotajewellers-para: A pioneer in the jewellery business, the Kota jewellers are a family run business in the jewellery business for the past four generations. We designed their showroom in the heart of the jewellery and commercial district in Coimbatore, where the original traders of the city had settled in, with a modern, well lit store and traditional detailing of warm wood, lighting and handpainted panels.
lighthouse-para: Light house is a residence set in the suburbs of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. We designed this house for a young couple who were busy entrepreneurs and their sons to create a beautiful house for them to grow together. Aptly named the lighthouse, the residence is punctured with light pockets that illuminate the house naturally and creates a beautiful play with light and texture.
lighthouse-para2: The design language of the house comes from tradition and artistic taste meeting contemporary architecture, where we wanted to create a house that highlighted comfort, luxury and tradition. This is showcased through the house, with pockets of nostalgia and family referred to across the residence. Bespoke custom murals, a gentle palette with muted tones and specific detailing across to reflect the tastes and interests of the members of the household. We played with a limited material board of wood, glass and marble to create the mood for this residence and used custom artwork, sculptures and furniture to accentuate the spaces.
mahapalace-para: Maha Palace Fitness Centre is a gym centre in Tiruppur, India that we designed and built in 2010.
mahilampoo-para: Mahilampoo is an apartment we designed in 2010 and constructed as developers. The apartment is known for the cross ventilation and modern form.
malli-para: This is another apartment we designed and developed in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.
mootram-para: The Mootram Veedu, which translates to the Courtyard House in tamil is a stunning residence located in the suburbs of Somanur, Tamil Nadu. The house is rooted in Tamizh tradition and vastu, feng shui adhered principles, with a warm, rich palette, resulting in a beautiful home for the client. We, at Vishwakarma have a signature use of the courtyard as our crux, and an energy point to plan our spaces around. The principal architect and founder, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan believes in the courtyard as a meeting point for the entire family, a gathering space as well as a meeting point for energy flow in the space. The courtyard, a connection to nature, architecturally acts as a flood light and ventilation, with the remaining functions of the home arching from the courtyard.
mootram-para2: The rich, warm palette of coppers, brass and deep reds and earth tones accentuate the traditional detailing and design we envisioned for the residence. We believe in handworked elements and attention to detailing yet keeping the residence as a minimalistic layout for functionality and maintenance. In summary, the Mootram Veedu is a residence that is auspicious, and has a reverence for tradition and function.
mootram2-para: The office we designed for Texmo is an intimate workspace and creative think tank space for their projects and ventures. Designed to be immersed in nature and a space to step away from the norm to create and ideate. The inspiration we drew from is a cabin in the woods.
oculus-para: The Oculus house is a signature style of our principal architect and founder, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan, with his minimalistic style of architecture and fine detailing to accentuate the architectural form. A purist in his style, combined with creativity and craftsmanship makes this house a true architectural marvel.
oculus-para2: The client is a family of four, with a background in lighting design and business wanted a space to grow their family in.
pralochnanew-para: Pralochna apparels is a showroom for textiles and apparels based out of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Specialsing in handloom and block print textiles and clothes, the brand is a staple in the city.
pralochnaold-para: Pralochna apparels is a showroom for textiles and apparels based out of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Specialsing in handloom and block print textiles and clothes, the brand is a staple in the city.
purplebay-para: Purple Bay is a sanitary wares showroom located at Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu that deals in luxury sanitwary and bathroom accessories. We designed this space to truly have an immersive, experiential experience for clients to come and see products.
sepiahouse-para: The Sepia house is a warm toned residence that is designed for a family in the suburbs of Coimbatore, India. A palette of beige, browns, and metal tones with handmade doors, furniture and hand painted furniture to accentuate the house.
attangudi-para: The Attangudi Veedu is a traditional residence designed for an entrepreneur and his family in Coimbatore. The house, located in the heart of a residential zone in south of Coimbatore, is worked with traditional detailing such as a temple altar constructed in granite, and pure wood carved furniture and cladding as well as handmade athangudi tiling. The residence is a homage to traditional tamizh architectural style.
soupandsaladaadyar-para: Soup and Salad is a chain of restaurants based out of Chennai, India. The ethos of the chain is rooted in conscious, mindful, healthy eating that compromises of contemporary takes on soups and salads, as the name suggests. We have designed each outlet with an ode to the history and cultural significance of the area in Chennai, with custom detailing and spatial qualities that reflect the unique area. In this restaurant, we opted for a more green, nature inspired detail that is reminiscent of the green streets of Adyar, which retains it quality of a quaint, older neighbourhood of chennai.
soupandsaladttk-para: Soup and Salad is a chain of restaurants based out of Chennai, India. The ethos of the chain is rooted in conscious, mindful, healthy eating that compromises of contemporary takes on soups and salads, as the name suggests. We have designed each outlet with an ode to the history and cultural significance of the area in Chennai, with custom detailing and spatial qualities that reflect the unique area. In this restaurant, we included murals of classical icons and musical elements to enrich the design. TTK road has a significance of traditional carnatic music because of the music academy which hosts the classical music festivals during the margazhali festival.
stackhouse-para: The Stack House is an interesting residence we designed in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu for a young entrepreneur and jeweller. He had a site that was very small in size, sandwiched between a multi-storey building and an empty site on the other side. The buildings across the street were mid level apartment buildings as well. The size of the plot was about 1200 sq ft and we had to design a residence for him as a single user with additions for future family.  With the site constraints, we decided to stack the programs of the space vertically, resulting in an interesting form and flow of spaces. The plan is stacked on top of each other, dividing and grouping the programs based on function and zoning of public to private.
stackhouse-para2: The Stack House is a typology of residence that is unique to the Coimbatore residential landscape. Since we are generous and blessed with more landspace, the houses more often lean towards a horizontal planning and this posed an interesting challenge for us. The design evolved into a 4 storey plan with a semi-basement garage that could house upto four cars and we tucked away all the services and amenities into the garage. The remaining floors were divided into public, semi-public and private zones, from ground floor to the second floor.
summerhouse-para: The Summer House is a space designed to relax and indulge in luxury while reconnecting with ourselves and the people around us. The client, Manoj came to us to design this house around 2020, as a weekend getaway property for his family to whisk away to on the weekends. The client and his family are industrialists who work in the garment and vegan product business with work shuffling them between Coimbatore, Tirupur and Kangayam, three industrial and enterprising cities in the west of Tamil Nadu. Since they have to keep travelling for work between the cities, came to us with a brief of creating a luxury farmhouse. Nestled in a 100 acre property that is lush with foliage, the house is perched amidst a grove of trees, farmland and their garment factory, resulting in beautiful views all around. A cow shed and duck pond are situated close to the property, and the children frolic and spend a large portion of their time there, with the animals and in the farm. There is a miniature version of a hand pump recreated for the kids to experiment and play and get a chance to see how it functions.
summerhouse-para2: The property leans on nature and outside spaces such as the veranda, spa, pool, garden and a play area for the children to shape the flow of spaces and character. Natural sunlight, open courtyards and details run through the house, creating memorable encounters at every turn. The use of a natural and neutral pallete at the Summer House, allows the surrounding landscape and the materials used to shine. The design language of the house comes from nostalgia meeting contemporary architecture, we wanted to create a house that highlighted comfort, luxury and tradition. This is showcased through the house, with personal artefacts and references to the clients background, such as the hand painted veena mounted below a glass ledge, creating a conversational piece. Another highlight is the feature wall, with cow masks and carvings as the clients son has an affinity to cows. The client, Manoj had two important briefs: natural light is key and their affinity towards courtyards. This fit in perfectly with the design language Karthikeyan, the principal architect and founder of Vishwakarma. The property is punctured with courtyards that flood light into the space, with wide walkways and passage ways around the courtyard, and using customized artisanal furniture that complete the space.
terrahouse-para: The Terra House is a rich residence designed in the suburbs of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu for a family of four who are industrialists and wanted a home that was immersed in nature and a getaway.
treehouse-para: The theme for this residence is the tree of life. All the detailing and designs are inspired by a tree, the source of life.
vasavitemple-para: The Vasavi temple is a temple revered and held in high regard by the Vysya community in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu and this project is an ongoing renovation of the temple structure and interiors with an addition of an community annex, with a mandapam ( wedding hall and venue) as well as rooms and a rooftop dining and intimate event space for the community.
veeduone-para: The office we designed for Texmo is an intimate workspace and creative think tank space for their projects and ventures. Designed to be immersed in nature and a space to step away from the norm to create and ideate. The inspiration we drew from is a cabin in the woods.
veedu2-para: The office we designed for Texmo is an intimate workspace and creative think tank space for their projects and ventures. Designed to be immersed in nature and a space to step away from the norm to create and ideate. The inspiration we drew from is a cabin in the woods.
veedu4-para: This is an intimate home designed for dear friends in Tiruppur, sparked with detailing, color and elements that spark the word home and family.
veedu6-para: This house was designed and constructed by us in the year 2009. The house has a more traditional,ornamental facade and a fun, colorful interior, with a lot of personalised, handcrafted furniture, all made in house by us.
victorianhouse-para: This residence is an opulent, rich residence that is ornate and detailed with heavy wooden detailing and paneling as well as rich, deep autumnal  palette of colors.
villanunc-para: Villa Nunc is another contemporary residence designed by us in Coimbatore, Tamil nadu.
yarnhouse-para: Set amidst the background of the industrial background of textiles, locks and agricultural machinery , Dindigul is a city in the heart of the southern part of Tamil Nadu. Dindigul is an ancient settlement, with many dynasties ruling over millennia, creating a rich history in the city. Set against this background, the Yarn House is a residence we created, weaving a beautiful space for a joint family who are in the spinning and textile business.  This residence is situated in their mill compound, serving as a gathering space for the entire family.
yarnhouse-para2: A spanning lavish home, with 5 bedrooms, a home gym, pool intersected by communal spaces and gathering points all connected to a focal courtyard which floods in natural light throughout the day. The spaces are linked through the design elements, with a contemporary take on traditional motifs and elements.  The principal architect and designer, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan, is a man of few words. His work speaks for itself and the Yarn House is an example of this. The design and spatial quality of the residence is immersed in the details with each room designed in a distinct yet succinct character with natural light,  cross ventilation that brings the residence alive.
ksir-para: KSIRS is a residential and day school based out of Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. We entered the design and planning phase of the property when there was an existing school block and the management wanted to expand to cater to higher education as well. The resulting design, a play of geometry and color is our vision for the new additions for the school, a beautiful learning platform.
balledoftime-para1: A Ballad of Time is an contemporary residence that was designed as an extension of a previous ancestral house that was built by the clients family over a span of 100 years. It is a beautiful piece of architecture that showcases the rich history of the Tamizh culture with houses built in 1920 and 1970 that are adjoined. We joined as the spatial designers and architects to add to the existing spaces for growing requirements of the family.
balledoftime-para2: Our chief architect, Karthikeyan took inspiration from the play of levels and courtyards present in traditional Tamizh architecture and designed the new residence with elements of space that intersect with light, volume and steps to create an inspired residence.
amodernsanctuary-para: A Modern Sanctuary is a cozy apartment in the heart of Coimbatore for a family of four, with a modern design, complete with all amenities and comfort. A true modern sanctuary.
stackedhouse-para1: The Layered house is a residential project nestled in the suburbs of Tamil Nadu, blending modern comfort and celebrating artistic Indian craftsmanship. The house is layered spatially, seamlessly blending the natural and built environments making it the perfect home for the family of four. The spatial planning involved stacking programs beside one another, with blurring the spaces to create a layered flow allowing the space to unfold. The clubhouse presents the opportunity to experience the natural environment and enter a relaxing atmosphere to entertain and host, complete with bedrooms and a pool.
stackedhouse-para2: Each room is designed and customized with design elements that weave the narrative of the house. Indian craftsmanship is showcased throughout the building, from the main door carved from wood, with brass motif tiles to a clay sculpture that spans across the balcony, handcrafted in the northern part of India. Leaves found near the local site were pressed into the walls to create imprints and the central pooja (prayer room) is wrapped with a traditional painting, depicting motifs depicted in temples. The house is a testimony to celebrating traditional Indian craftsmanship and will hold witness to the people who live there as well as the craft.
fluidharmony-para: This is a residence nestled in the suburbs of Coimbatore with the glorious Western Ghats as the backdrop. It is designed and constructed by Vishwakarma Design Studio, in our classic courtyard style - which Karthikeyan, our founder and principal architect coins together subtly in aesthetics and functionality. The residence is furnished with warm tones of polished wood, all designed and made in our studio, in Coimbatore and we designed each room and space with clarity, functionality and the clients tastes.
veedu9-para: Veedu #9 is an artistically designed house that fits a family of four, in the nestling busy Race Course area of Coimbatore. We programmatically arranged the needs of the family to include their day to day activities and life, blended with artistic touches.
turya-detail-para: A set of coasters, with handcarved wood and polished,with beaten copper motifs, thematic with natural elements and designs that are handsketched.
journal-mainpage-thought1-para: Join us to hear more about our founders thoughts on architecture, design and life. Kathikeyan Padmanabhan, a seasoned practioner embodies a wholistic practice of art, architecture, philosophy and spirituality in his profession.

journal-mainpage-thought2-para: What establishes the Genus Loci of a place? Read more to discover our thoughts on the soul of space.

journal-mainpage-text2-head1: WE LOOK AT EVERY DESIGN THROUGH THE HEART AND THE HEAD.
journal-mainpage-publications2-para: Century Apparels, a state of the art garment factory and corporate office designed  in Tamil Nadu, showcased Society Interiors.
journal-mainpage-design1-para: One of the things we are most proud of in our design practice is the handcrafted, unique designs we give birth to and bring life. We handsketch and curate buildings, spaces and furniture on every scale. When we put as much detail into every aspect of our design, it creates beautiful results...
journal-mainpage-thought3-para: The staircase, referred to as the symbolic spine of the house is the core around which a lot of the spaces and functions revolve...
journal-mainpage-publications3-para: Coimbatore based architects Karthick and his wife Ruckmani's home Turya, combines a resort-like feeling with the sophestication of a modern contemporary house...
journal-mainpage-recognitions3-para: Our principal architect Karthikeyan Padmanabhan and managing director Ruckmini Karthikeyan addressed the students about running an architectural practice and how to design with heart and soul.
journal-mainpage-publications4-para: We designed this house for a young couple who are busy entrepreneurs and their sons to create a beautiful house for them to grow together...
journal-mainpage-thought4-para: Materiality and tactility is crucial in evoking this multi sensorial experience in space.

journal-thought1-para1: Our founder and principal architectural designer, Karthikeyan Padmanabhans reflects on design and architecture, and a snippet of how he views the world around him.
journal-thought1-para2: Growing up, a large part of my childhood was me with my paper and color pencils, creating the world around me onto paper with vivid illustrations as well as my imagination into sketches and paintings. I grew up in a fast paced household, with a big joint family and with my father being a doctor who travelled and kept shifting bases, I got the opportunity to see multiple places and cultures intimately in their varying forms, shapes and beliefs. I moved fluidly between the spaces as they kept morphing into cities, rural villages, the mountains, the seaside with the anchor of my grandmothers ancestral home in the heart of southern Tamil Nadu, Kumbakonam which is a cradle of warmth, comfort amidst an amalgamation of  culture, religion, art and lush agricultural fields on the banks of Cauvery.
journal-thought1-para3: All these experiences add to who I am today as a designer and it is very much reflected in what we create at Vishwakarma Design Studio. The connection and powerful relationship between the built and natural environment is the crux of our practice and I strive to foster the connection between humans and nature through architecture.
journal-thought1-para4: People and their stories also fascinate me. As an architect and designer, I often get glimpses and whispers of people and what makes them who they are. It is a beautiful to craft spaces that speak to them, and their dreams and hopes.
journal-thought1-para5: I realise that life is an journey of experiences, an amalgamation of moments, memories and encounters and that the spaces, buildings and products we create are stamped in the universe by time, life breathed in by the users, and stay far after we, the architects have created, travelling through time, coexisting with nature and science, narrating our stories, reflecting the artist in us, an uninterrupted flow of creation...
journal-recognitions3-para1: Our principal architect and founder, Karthikeyan had the pleasure of addressing the topic 'Discovering the Soul of Architecture' at the Design Perspective held at Coimbatore. The line up had an impressive lineup of established professionals and designers at the conference with interesting guest speakers and industry members.
journal-recognitions3-para2: We spoke about the importance of 'Genus Loci' which is the spirit of a place and how architects play a crucial role in creating the spirit of a place. Emotional and multi-sensory architecture is an integral part in how we design at our studio and this seemed like a fitting topic to address to the audience.
journal-recognitions3-para3: Stay tuned to see more about what we are upto and other topics such as the 'Spirit of Architecture' and more!
journal-thought3-para1: What establishes the Genus Loci of a place? It is the intangible quality that turns a space into a place, something that has a belonging, which is established through a various number of factors such as volume, materiality, colour, light, landscape, art and spirit.
journal-thought3-para2: As an architect and designer, establishing and integrating spirit and place is one of the most honouring journeys and at here Vishwakarmadesignstudio , we take this role very seriously.
journal-thought3-para3: The buildings and spaces we design are sacred and we believe that the energy of the space is key for prosperity and abundance. As a design practitioner, considering the #Genusloci of a space is an interesting design consideration and how it shapes the design and planning of our projects. It makes way for interesting and surprising process of discovery, which results in unique designs for our clients.
journal-recognitions2-para1: Vishwakarma Design Studio recently had the honour of being presented with the "Outstanding & Prominent Architecture & Interior Design Firm of the Year 2023 under Residential Projects & Commercial Projects and Trusted Architect & Designer of the Year 2023! We are very excited and humbled to be included in this space. Our principal architects and founders, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan and Ruckmini Karthikeyan received the prestigious award.
journal-design1-para1: Artisanal design. We work with a lot of native artisans in our architectural and interior design. Over the past 30 years we have had the opportunity and privilege to meet incredible artists, craftsman that have shown immense skill and talent which have translated into our projects as well.
journal-design1-para2: Why do we work with artisans? The first reason being that it resonates with the ethos of our firm. From the beginning, we believe that design and spaces are personal and should reflect a deep belonging. A belonging to the space and its users is the life force of the building or space. By infusing our designs with artisanal design, it creates belonging and context to the design.
journal-design1-para3: The next reason is to bring livelihoods to the artisans. A lot of marginalised and dwindling groups get exposure and livelihoods through the work on the projects we do. We believe in trying to source locally for environmental and social consciousness as responsible entrepreneurs and designers.
journal-design1-para4: Finally, we'd like to conclude this by adding that India is a vast and culturally diverse country with a lot of different artistic styles and forms of art and design. We get to celebrate our cultural tapestry through our profession which brings us pride.
journal-design3-para1: How did Turya come to be?
journal-design3-para2: Turya, is defined as the pure consciousness of the universe in Sanskrit, the state of being beyond the mortal realms. The individual soul realizes and transcends the three states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep consciousness in turya. While the word has a deep spiritual meaning and is rooted in Indian culture, we named our furniture platform Turya to represent the designs and furniture we create as one of a kind and out of this world. When we design, it is spiritual to us as we design from within, by looking within and then drawing from the outside. Design is a holistic process at our studio and hence Turya was born.
journal-design3-para3: We design all types of products and design furniture, lifestyle products in a multidisciplinary platform by combining wood, glass, metal and paint to create stunning pieces of art that are one of a kind. Over the past 30 years we have carved a niche for ourselves as one of the leading and pioneers in creating custom pieces of furniture and products in South India. Our founders, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan and Ruckmini Karthikeyan began Turya as a young couple in 1995, at the inception of their design profession. Down the road, they began Vishwakarma Design Studio as their construction, architectural and design platform and Turya remained their product and furniture platform. Together, we create a complete, holistic brand entity for your building needs.
journal-design2-para2: How do we design at our studio? Our principal architect and founder, Karthikeyan Padmanabhan still believes in putting pen to paper and he personally hand sketches all our designs and then they are converted into digital drawings and 3D visualizations for our presentations. He believes that his creative process is at its purest when he sits down and designs on paper and our designs speak to this. We create a lot more unique designs that sing with soul when we design on paper. Featured here are a few of the sketches by Ar. Karthikeyan.

journal-recognitions1-para3:
We also highlighted our journey as architects and designers and personal anecdotes to the faculty and students.
It was lovely to interact with the faculty and students and share a little about our practice. Thank you for having us.
journal-recognitions4-para1: This residence was nominated for the best use of color at the WADE ASIA festival this year. While we did not win the award, we are extremely grateful for the opportunity to present the project and share a project that is so close to our hearts for so many reasons.
journal-recognitions4-para2: Each opportunity presents a chance to learn something about ourselves and we took away some very thoughtful insights in this experience.
journal-recognitions4-para3: 1. There is always room for improvement. While design is largely subjective, this experience really showed us to look at different sides and opinions. As a practice, we often don't hear criticisms on our design. ( this took us right back to the jury days in college)
journal-recognitions4-para4: 2. The opportunity to learn and see other architects and designers present their projects. This was the most enriching part of this conference, as we got to see so many wonderful projects that inspired us!
journal-recognitions4-para5: 3. We saw different ways to even present our project. While we loved the presentation we had made, it was enriching and heartening to see one designer bring the gond artisan who worked on the mural with her and have her speak on stage and share her design process.We have worked with Gond artists extensively in the Color House as well and this opened a new avenue of thinking for us.
journal-recognitions4-para6: All in all, it was a great experience and we loved creating this home and it is near and dear to our hearts and the Color House being nominated was a honor.
journal-thought4-para1: Let's talk about materiality in architecture and design. Juhani Pallasma famously said that the 'eyes are the skin in architecture' , we touch and see a place through the eyes first, we take in the world around us through the eyes first.
journal-thought4-para2: Although architecture and spatial design has traditionally been viewed as an ocularcentric profession, limiting the role of sight to just what is seen in space but the eyes go beyond the function of vision, evoking a multi-sensorial experience of touch, feel, memory, smell and taste as well.  Materiality and tactility is crucial in evoking this multi sensorial experience in space.
journal-thought4-para3: What are your thoughts about materiality and multisensorial architecture?
journal-thought2-para1: The staircase, a transitory space from one level to another in building design. In our studio, we look at this transitory space as an opportunity to design another aspect of a space that can infuse more life into what we envision for the space.
journal-thought2-para2: The staircase, referred to as 'the symbolic spine of the house' is the core around which a lot of the spaces and functions revolve. We create to qualitatively and quantitatively add to functional space to make it holistic, functional and aesthetic.

journal-planning1-para1: How do we spatially plan and design?
journal-planning1-para2: This is a very wide and large subject to approach in design, how do we design and create? We aim to give a small insight into the topic by some of the key considerations we take as well as reflecting on ethos and principles at our practice as well.
journal-planning1-para3: 1. Light - Light is the primary and most instinctive principle we have in our practice. The inclusion of natural light is crucial to emotional, mental and physical wellbeing. Light is held sacred and breathes life into all living beings. We create with light as the focus in our design and planning.
journal-planning1-para4: 2. Natural Ventilation - Natural ventilation and circulation of fresh air is crucial in our design and planning. Vernacular architecture is the usage of local materials and adapting to the local environment and climate when designing a building, another core principle in our design
journal-planning1-para5: 3. Central circulation - One of the iconic features we are known for are the courtyards we include in our spatial planning. The courtyard has an intangible quality that is nostalgic, and a nod to the old style of traditional architecture in India as well as the influx of light and air that is brought in through a courtyard. The central courtyard also informs the circulation in a space and evokes everyone to the focal point as a gathering space.
journal-planning1-para6: 4. Designer - When we say designer, we mean that each space has an unique spatial quality architecturally and in interiors. We carve design identities for each building, home or space we design and that we are proud to say that no two buildings have the same design.
journal-planning1-para7: 5. Familiarity - A space has the power to evoke memories, to make someone feel safe, to be a source of inspiration. Creating a space with intention is important to us.
journal-planning1-para8: 6. Love - All our work is from the heart, we put our soul and effort into creating for our clients and for ourselves. We believe that when we create from a source of love, we cannot go wrong.
journal-planning1-para9: 7. Functionality - It goes without saying that functionality is integral to any design. Functionality meeting aesthetics is the fine line a designer plays in spatial planning.
journal-planning1-para10: 8. Scale and ratio - This is an important aspect of design, where scale, proportion and ratio are important considerations while designing a space. How elements interact with one another, the meaning and context they give to each other should be focused on.
journal-planning2-para2: What is the relationship between architecture and the environment?
journal-planning2-para3: There is a symbiotic, intrinsic relationship between architecture and the environment. The natural environment informs the architect about the building and it allows us to shape the space around. We need to build around the environment as opposed to forcing a building into the environment. Listening to the wisdom of a place or site is what respecting the land is. Architecture that is kind to the environment is the need of the hour, and at our practice we inspire and aspire to include the natural environment as much as possible in our designs. This is the first and primary step that we take is to ensure the inclusion of the natural environment, through landscape, interior gardens and retaining the existing landscape as much as possible. This ensures the emotional and mental wellbeing and increases the oxygen levels, leading to overall wellbeing of the users.
journal-planning2-para4: Materiality. How can we be mindful of the usage of materiality in design and building? In vernacular architecture, we use local materials and the context of local climate to dictate the form and materiality to adapt to the surrounding environment. It is also sustainable in terms of ones carbon footprint by procuring materials that are local. While this cant be adhered to a 100% due to a number of external factors, as professionals we strive to use locally sourced materials when possible.
journal-planning2-para5: The essence of a building in architecture. We look at the soil, the wind patterns, the sun path to design our buildings, which inform us the openings, how the flow of spaces will be, the circulation to design luxury buildings and spaces. This also shows us the placement of spaces like bathrooms where the sunlight is high and eliminating the need for artificial lighting and ventilation whenever and wherever required. It also ensures that we can design for the needs of our clientele and that we can design sustainably.
journal-planning2-para6: Looking at the Earth as "ancestoral" and "technology" as the future. The Earth is something we've inherited, deserving of the respect and care. The Earth, every species, flora and fauna has to be revered and when we look at it as generational wealth that is passed down. When this awareness seeps in, architecture, design and construction considerably shifts and we begin to be more mindful of the impact we have on the earth. Now, as technology keeps growing and increasingly becomes an integral part of our lives, we invite you to think how we can design with more sensitivity using this technology to pay homage to our traditions and our roots.
